title: Trusted Types sinks use this's relevant global object, but engines use the node document's
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

HTML's Trusted Types sinks pass *this*'s relevant global object, which doesn't change when an element is adopted into another document. For example, `Element`'s `innerHTML` setter:

> Let (*compliantString*, *compliantOptions*) be the result of invoking the get trusted type compliant input algorithm with this's relevant global object, the given value, ...

`setHTMLUnsafe()`, `insertAdjacentHTML()`, `HTMLScriptElement`'s `src`, etc. do the same.

Trusted Types' own attribute handling uses the node document instead ([get trusted type compliant attribute value](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-attribute-value)):

> *element*'s node document's relevant global object as *global*

Chrome Canary, Firefox Nightly and Safari TP seem to use the node document for the HTML sinks too. Given a document with `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` and a same-origin iframe without it, calling `innerHTML`, `setHTMLUnsafe()` and `insertAdjacentHTML()` with a string from the iframe's realm:

- throws a `TypeError` for a `div` created in the iframe and adopted into the TT document, and
- doesn't throw for a `div` created in the TT document and adopted into the iframe's document.

The `trusted-types/Element-setAttribute-respects-Elements-node-documents-globals-CSP-after-adoption-*` tests check the same thing for attributes.

Maybe HTML's sinks should use this's node document's relevant global object instead, to match engines and Trusted Types' attribute handling. (Found in #12758.)
